---
title: "Apple Stock - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Introduction:

We are going to use Apple's stock price.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/09_Time_Series/Apple_Stock/appl_1980_2014.csv)

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable apple

```{r}
# the same file is also included in this folder: read_csv("appl_1980_2014.csv")
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/09_Time_Series/Apple_Stock/appl_1980_2014.csv"

# col_types reads Date as text (and the rest as numbers) so that we convert the dates ourselves
apple <- read_csv(url, col_types = cols(Date = col_character(), .default = col_double()))

head(apple)
```

### Step 4. Check out the type of the columns

```{r}
sapply(apple, class)
```

### Step 5. Transform the Date column as a date type

```{r}
apple <- apple |> mutate(Date = ymd(Date))

head(apple$Date)
```

### Step 6. Set the date as the index

```{r}
# tibbles have no index: we keep Date as the first column
apple <- apple |> relocate(Date)

head(apple)
```

### Step 7. Is there any duplicate dates?

```{r}
# NO! All are unique
any(duplicated(apple$Date))
```

### Step 8. Ops...it seems the data is ordered from the most recent date. Make the first entry the oldest date.

```{r}
apple <- apple |> arrange(Date)
head(apple)
```

### Step 9. Get the last business day of each month

```{r}
apple_month <- apple |>
  group_by(month = floor_date(Date, "month")) |>
  # the last day with data of each month is its last business (trading) day
  filter(Date == max(Date)) |>
  ungroup()

head(apple_month)

# if you want the mean of each month instead (like resample('BM').mean() in pandas):
# apple |> group_by(month = floor_date(Date, "month")) |> summarise(across(-Date, mean))
```

### Step 10. What is the difference in days between the first day and the oldest

```{r}
as.numeric(max(apple$Date) - min(apple$Date))
```

### Step 11. How many months in the data we have?

```{r}
n_distinct(floor_date(apple$Date, "month"))
```

### Step 12. Plot the 'Adj Close' value. Set the size of the figure to 13.5 x 9 inches

```{r fig.width=13.5, fig.height=9}
# the size of the figure is set in the chunk options: fig.width and fig.height
ggplot(apple, aes(x = Date, y = `Adj Close`)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Apple Stock")

# to save it to a file with that size:
# ggsave("apple.png", width = 13.5, height = 9)
```
